sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic laws, crossings, lane markings and right of way

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Delaware prohibits texting and handheld phone use while driving; phone conversations require hands-free equipment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
A driver may dial or activate or deactivate wireless equipment, then must set the device down. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
The driving restriction also covers handheld electronic communication devices such as pagers, portable computers and two-way communication devices. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A01
A driver holding a GDL may not use a phone or electronic device while driving, even hands-free. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A01
Authorized emergency-vehicle operators performing official duties and people reporting emergencies are excepted from the device-use restriction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A01
The device-use exemptions include operators of farm tractors, unregistered farm trucks or farm equipment, and HAM radio operators. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A01
A business or government employee may use an attached or mounted two-way vehicle radio to communicate with dispatch, a base or other employees under the listed exemption. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A01
A driver must communicate an intended stop, turn or lane change by hand signal or turn signal 300 feet before the action. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A01
When passing to the left, keep a safe distance and return right only after safely clearing the other vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A01
Passing a cyclist requires at least three feet of clearance throughout the pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A01
On a multilane road, a driver passing a cyclist must use the neighboring lane whenever possible. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A01
A vehicle being passed must give way right and avoid accelerating until the pass is complete. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0081]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A02
For an approaching authorized emergency vehicle using a siren or the listed alternating red-light combinations, yield and move immediately to the right edge clear of intersections until it passes, unless police direct otherwise. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A02
The approaching-emergency-vehicle law also extends to DelDOT operators requested to support police or fire personnel at an incident. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A02
When approaching a stationary emergency, DelDOT, tow or other vehicle giving the described warnings, proceed cautiously and change lanes to yield when possible. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A02
If moving over would be unsafe or impossible, proceed carefully and slow to a safe speed. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A02
The listed alternating warning colors for stationary emergency vehicles are red alone, blue alone, blue paired with white, red paired with white or blue, and the red-white-blue combination. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A02
The stationary DelDOT warning described in the move-over rule uses alternating amber or red-and-amber lights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A02
The stationary tow-truck warning described in the move-over rule uses alternating amber, white or amber-and-white lights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A02
The move-over rule also includes a stationary vehicle displaying hazard lights, flares, cones, caution signs or other nonvehicle warning signs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A02
On a multilane roadway, move one lane away from a stopped vehicle until safely beyond it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A02
On a two-lane roadway, slow below the posted limit until completely beyond the stopped vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A03
Delaware traffic laws apply to all highway users, including drivers, cyclists, people guiding vehicles or riding animals, and pedestrians. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A03
Follow a police officer’s instructions even when they conflict with signs, signals, markings or usual traffic laws. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A03
Do not bypass a traffic sign or signal by leaving the roadway and crossing private property. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A03
Every grade crossing has an emergency dispatch number for reporting crossing, track or train problems to the railroad. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A03
The railroad emergency notification number is normally on a blue sign at the crossbuck or near the crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F28 | anchor: A03
The ENS sign’s DOT number identifies the crossing location for responders and railroad personnel. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F29 | anchor: A03
Giving the dispatcher the crossing’s DOT number helps locate a blockage so approaching trains can be slowed or stopped. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F30 | anchor: A03
Never attempt to race a train through a railroad crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F31 | anchor: A03
Do not start across tracks unless the far side has enough room for the entire vehicle without stopping on the tracks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F32 | anchor: A03
The handbook recommends avoiding gear changes while traversing tracks because of the risk of stalling. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F33 | anchor: A04
The advance railroad warning is a round yellow sign bearing a black X and RR letters. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F34 | anchor: A04
Rail-crossing advance pavement markings commonly contain an X, RR letters and a stopping bar. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F35 | anchor: A04
A white X-shaped railroad crossbuck has the meaning of a yield sign and requires yielding to trains. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F36 | anchor: A04
Flashing side-by-side railroad-crossing lights require a stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F37 | anchor: A04
Never drive around a lowered railroad gate. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F38 | anchor: A04
Where a crossing bell sounds, do not cross until it stops. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F39 | anchor: A04
A track-count sign warns of multiple tracks and possible additional trains; even without one, check for more than one track. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F40 | anchor: A04
A solid white road-edge line identifies the outer edge of the travel lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F41 | anchor: A04
White lane markings separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F42 | anchor: A04
A broken white lane line may be crossed for a safe lane change. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F43 | anchor: A04
A single solid white lane line discourages changing lanes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F44 | anchor: A04
A double solid white lane line prohibits changing lanes. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F45 | anchor: A04
When a sign or signal requires stopping, stop before reaching the stopping line or crosswalk. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F46 | anchor: A05
A crosswalk can exist without painted markings, so remain alert for pedestrians at intersections. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F47 | anchor: A05
Yellow lines separate opposing directions of traffic. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F48 | anchor: A05
A broken yellow center line may be crossed to pass when safe. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F49 | anchor: A05
Where opposing lanes have one solid and one broken yellow line, passing is prohibited from the solid-line side. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F50 | anchor: A05
Where a solid and broken yellow line are paired, a driver on the broken-line side may pass safely. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F51 | anchor: A05
Two solid yellow center lines prohibit passing from either direction. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F52 | anchor: A05
A solid yellow line may be crossed for a safe turn into a driveway. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F53 | anchor: A05
Reversible lanes change travel direction at different times and are normally marked with paired broken yellow lines; check which lane is available before entering. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F54 | anchor: A05
A green arrow above a reversible lane allows use of that lane. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F55 | anchor: A05
A red X above a reversible lane prohibits its use. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F56 | anchor: A05
A steady yellow X means lane use is changing; leave the lane as soon as safely possible. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F57 | anchor: A05
A lane marked Transit or Bus is reserved for buses, while a Bicycle designation reserves it for bicycles. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F58 | anchor: A05
HOV signs specify the required number of occupants and applicable times; HOV 3 requires at least three people in the vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F59 | anchor: A05
A roundabout moves traffic counterclockwise around a central island. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0085]

Misconceptions: Preserve the source’s conditions, exceptions and may-versus-must distinction when recalling a rule.
Mnemonics: Use “cause, condition, consequence” as an authored cue for reviewing each cited rule.
Glossary: The key source terms are retained in the individual facts and their domain labels.
Dynamic facts: Contact details, provider lists and current service availability require fresh confirmation and stay outside the stable fact set.
